How deep is the depth of seasonal movement?
The foundation level should be no closer than 2–2.5 m to the ground surface: below this depth the water content no longer changes with the seasons.
When does damage caused by expansive clay typically appear?
When the snow melts in spring
After a long dry summer, especially after several dry years
During a flood
During a long frost
The damage typically appears after a long dry summer, especially if several dry years follow one another.
What percentage of the damage affects single-storey buildings?
83% of the damage occurs in single-storey, 13% in two-storey and 4% in three-storey buildings: the small load cannot counteract the swelling.
Which clay mineral swells most strongly?
Water enters between the layers of montmorillonite (smectite), so it swells strongly. A high montmorillonite and illite content is characteristic of expansive clay.
Why is a high contact pressure favourable on expansive clay?
Because it counteracts the swelling pressure, so the soil cannot lift the building
Because it speeds up consolidation
Because it takes the footing below the frost depth
The bearing resistance of the ground should be used as fully as possible: the higher the contact pressure, the less the swelling pressure can lift the building.
Which is the worst solution on such ground?
A full basement
A partial basement
A reinforced strip footing 2.5 m deep
Pad footings with ground beams, 2.5 m deep
A partial basement is the worst: the part with the basement stands deep, in undisturbed soil, while the rest is in the moving zone. The result is uneven movement and cracking.
How should “wet” services be brought into the building?
Parallel to the wall
Perpendicular to the wall, through an oval, sealed opening, in a sleeve
Diagonally under the floor
The connections should be perpendicular to the wall, and relative movement between the pipe and the wall must be possible.
Which three factors must be present together for collapse?
Drought, load, clay
Collapsible soil, load and water
Water, frost, loess
Load, temperature, water
Collapse requires collapsible soil, load and water to be present together.
When is a soil at risk of collapse?
The collapse coefficient is iᵣ = Δh/h; if it exceeds 0.01 (1%), the soil is at risk of collapse.
Does widening the footing protect the building from collapse?
Yes, because the contact pressure decreases
No: if all three conditions are met, increasing the safety against bearing failure does not help either
Only for footings wider than 2 m
Only in sandy loess
If all three conditions are met, the building cannot be protected from rapid, sudden settlement by increasing the safety against bearing failure (by widening the footing).
How much of Hungary is covered by loess?
About 1/3
About 2/3
About a third of Hungary is covered by loess, so collapse is a particularly important issue here.
What should be done in rainy weather after the foundation trench has been excavated?
Wait until it dries out
Concrete straight away, or remove the soaked soil
Cover it and leave it for a week
Wash it in with water and compact it
After excavation, concreting must start straight away, or the soaked soil below foundation level must be removed.
Which method is NOT one of the ground improvement methods used for collapsible soils?
Dropped tamping plate
Vibroflotation
Stabilisation with sodium silicate
Ground freezing
Methods used for collapsible soil: dropped tamping plate, vibroflotation, stabilisation with sodium silicate, soil burning, flooding + preloading.
What is the aim of flooding + preloading?
To dry out the soil
To force collapse in advance, before construction
To raise the groundwater level
To dissolve the lime
With flooding and preloading, collapse is forced in advance, before the structure is completed.
Which fill is the most dangerous?
50-year-old, compacted sandy gravel
Household waste, or uncompacted fill less than 8–10 years old
Old, mixed soil
Compacted crushed concrete
Household waste (municipal waste) and uncompacted fill less than 8–10 years old are very dangerous.
What percentage of the damaged floors in Hungary stood on fill?
40% of the damaged structural elements, 57% of the partition walls and 70% of the floors stood on fill.
What share of the damage related to made ground was triggered by water?
87% of the damage was triggered by water (broken sewers, roof water, burst pressure pipes, surface water).
What contact pressure should not be exceeded on made ground?
There is no limit
According to the design guideline, the contact pressure should not exceed 150–200 kPa.
What layer thickness can be compacted with a vibratory roller?
A plate compactor can compact layers 10–30 cm thick, a vibratory roller 30–50 cm, and a dropped tamping plate 2–4 m.
How should cement grouting be carried out in made ground?
From the bottom upwards
From the top downwards
Only from horizontal holes
The order does not matter
Cement grouting with a small amount of bentonite should be carried out from the top downwards.
Where can soil replacement be carried out?
Only above the groundwater level
Only below the groundwater level
Regardless of the groundwater
